title: Launch authorization and phase auto-advance contract
goal: Make mission launch authorization carry through the assessment chain so operators are not forced to re-confirm every phase when they already selected and authorized the intended depth at launch.
scope: Fix the operator contract around Full / all-phases launch, phase gates, auto-advance, and authorization visibility. If an operator selects a profile/depth that explicitly authorizes later phases, the chain should automatically continue through the authorized non-exploitation phases when prerequisites are met. Any remaining gate must explain exactly why it still requires confirmation, such as missing credentials, missing prerequisite evidence, out-of-scope expansion, destructive/intrusive exploitation, or a safety boundary. The UI must show which phases are pre-authorized, which are pending, and what will run next without requiring repeated guesswork.
generation_reason: Operator feedback after repo-state push: per-phase confirmation after already authorizing a full mission is confusing and inefficient. The system must preserve safety gates while honoring launch-time authorization and explaining any remaining required approval.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Only fix launch-time authorization carry-through, phase auto-advance clarity, and remaining-gate explanations. Do not bypass pack validation, runtime binding, scope enforcement, kill switch, credential prerequisites, or explicit exploitation authorization.

success_criteria: A Full / all-phases mission launched with explicit authorization records a durable authorization summary that Mission Control can display.
Authorized non-exploitation phases auto-advance when prerequisites are satisfied instead of asking the operator to confirm the same intent again.

Any phase that still blocks shows the exact reason and the safe next action: missing credential, missing finding/evidence prerequisite, missing tool readiness, scope expansion, intrusive exploitation, or failed runner review.
Wizard preview clearly states which phases will auto-advance after launch and which phase types can still require manual approval.
Mission Control phase cards distinguish pre-authorized, auto-advancing, waiting-on-prerequisite, and manual-approval-required states.
Tests cover Full Internal LAN / full-depth launch, no-credentials launch, credentialed launch, and exploitation-gated launch behavior without weakening safety boundaries.

acceptance_criteria: Full Internal LAN with launch-time authorization does not ask for redundant phase confirmations for already-authorized non-exploitation phases.
A no-credentials mission explains credential-dependent gates instead of silently skipping or repeatedly asking for approval.
Intrusive exploitation remains explicitly gated unless the launch flow recorded a specific exploitation authorization that satisfies the existing safety contract.
Mission Control shows what is authorized, what is next, and why anything is blocked.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the only active task.
after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Broad Mission Control redesign beyond the authorization/phase contract
Running live customer or intrusive targets
Weakening explicit exploitation, credential, scope, or kill-switch gates
